Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT S. Z009— 20 January 2009 MR. FEUMON SENO, ET AL Punong Barangay, Tapuyan Gasan, Marinduque Dear PB Seöo, et al: This has reference to your earlier letter seeking for our legal opinion, primarily on whether Punong Barangays and the Sangguniang Kabataan thereat may be compelled by the Mayor and the Pambayang Pederasyon ng Sangguniang Kabataan (PPSK) via the issuance of Memorandum No. OM- 2008-215 and PPSK Resolution No. 01 dated 17 May 2008, respectively, to contribute Five Thousand Pesos (Php5, 000.00) chargeable to whatever available fund of the SK as financial assistance to the sports competition (e.g. basketball tournament) sponsored by the municipal government and the PPSK. Per your letter and its attachments, last August 2008, the municipal government and the PPSK thereat had sponsored an SK Inter Barangay Basketball Tournament as part of the celebration of the 399th anniversary of the establishment of your town. In order to ensure the success of the sports competition, the PPSK passed PPSK Resolution No. 01, dated 17 May 2008, series of 2008, setting the amount of Php5, 000.00 as contribution/financial assistance of each Sangguniang Kabataan within the municipality. Thereafter, Mayor Victoria Lao Lim issued Memorandum No. OM- 2008-21, dated 24 June 2008, directing all concerned Punong Barangays and SK Chairmen, that Municipality, to remit their Php5, 000.00 contribution to the Sangguniang Kabataan through the Office of the Municipal Treasurer. In case the SK has not yet made an appropriation for the aforesaid amount, the Punong Barangays and the SK Chairmen are further advised to make the appropriation towards that end. Moreover, in case of

-2- failure, Mayor Lao Lim will be constrained to file appropriate administrative charges against those concerned. Thus, you are now seeking our legal opinion on these queries, which we quoted in toto, viz: "H "ich threat of administrative charges against us if we did not f011011• her orders under Memo No. OM-2008-215, is the action of the Mayor to compel us to pay the Php5,OOO from the SK fund proper, in order and not against the law? Is not the SK Council's budgeting decisions independent of the Mayor's control or for that matter even the SK Federation's control? Can the SK Federation's vote to support a project of the Mayor with a budgetary outlay coming not from the funds of the Federation but from individual SK Council's be binding on all SK councils? Can the Mayor sanction SK councils or even barangay councils who do not agree to pay this out of their individual SK Council or individual barangay fund. " In your letter, you also enumerated the following points for our consideration: 1) The Pun ong Baran ways ere n ot party to th e PPSK Resolution; 2) The PPSK members which are composed of the SK chairmen of each barangay had no prior resolution from their respective SK council to commit the P5,ooo contribution from the SK fimd the barangay; 3) The PPSK is an organiza tion of SK chairm en a t th e municipal level which has its own officers and governed by its constitution and by—laws. The act of each individual member SK chairman does not commit the whole barangay SK council without any resolution from the SK council, especially if this concerns the fund Of the barangay SK because there are government budgeting, accounting and auditing rules that need to be followed. The Federation is a totally difFerent entity from the commitment of its SK chairman who is the member of the Federation without prior authorization through a resolution from each SK council. If the funds concerned are funds of the Federation itself, then there should be no problem.- However, the fimds in this case are to be sourced from each barangay SK funds. 4) Moreover, th ere is n o Mem orandum Of Ag reement entered into by the PPSK and the Municipal Government of • Gasan that should bind the PPSK; 5) Hence, the contribution appears to be personal commitment of each SK Chairman and should not bind the barangay and the SK council.

-3- Before answering your queries, allow us first to explain the nature of the SK Fund and the procedure and manner by which the same is to be spent. Section 329 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) mandates that "ten percent (10%) of the general fund of the barangay shall be set aside for the sangguniang kabataan," which, in our opinion, means that such fund shall be included in the barangay budget as a lump sum amount and transferred to the account of the SK as a trust fund which may be deposited with the city or municipal treasury or any depository bank. Article 423 of the Rules and Regulations Implementing the Local Government Code of 1991 further provides that "the said ten percent share shall be appropriated and administered by the sangguniang kabataan and shall be spent for the purposes provided in Rule XXVII of [these] Rules except for personal services." Hence, the Punong Barangay has no control over the appropriation and administration of the SK Fund. In fact, under Section 389 the Punong Barangay only exercises general supervision over the activities of the sangguniang kabataan. And, as to what activities/purposes the SK fund shall be spent, note that vital and most important to the powers and functions of the Sangguniang Kabataan under Rule XXVII of the Rules and Regulations Implementing the Local Government Code is the enhancement of programs towards the members' social, political, economic, cultural, intellectual, moral and physical development. Before the SK fund is withdrawn or disbursed, the. same must be in accordance with the approved budget of the sangguniang kabataan pursuant to Section 433 of the Local Government Code of 1991. However, it may be observed that in practice, the approved budget of the Sangguniang Kabataan only set out purposes (for which the fund will be disbursed) in general terms, for example, the amount earmarked for sports development is twenty thousand pesos (Php 20, 000.00), for health is ten thousand pesos (PhpIO,OOO.OO). In order to ensure that the purpose for which the fund will be disbursed is in accordance with the purpose as set out in the budget: a Resolution validly passed by the Sangguniang Kabataan earmarking a certain amount for such purpose/activity is required before disbursement is made. Along this line, we fully agree with you that the Sangguniang Kabataan and the PPSK are separate organizations. The Sangguniang Kabataan is composed of the SK Chairman and seven (7) members while the PPSK is composed of the sangguniang kabataan chairmen of Barangays in the municipality. Section 1 (2) of the 2001 Katipunan ng

-4- Kabataan and Sangguniang Kabataan Constitution and By-Laws states that the SK Federation at all levels, including herein Pambayang Pederasyon ng Sangguniang Kabataan, have their own funds, which they can appropriate and administer. This goes without saying that the statement made in the 2nd Whereas Clause of PPSK Resolution No. 1, series of 2008 saying that the PPSK has no fund of its own is incorrect. Going now to your queries, we observed that a provision in the subject PPSK Resolution No. 01, series of 2008 categorically declared that the amount of Php5, 000.00-contribution/financial assistance of each member barangay was agreed upon. Such agreement shall bind therefore all Sangguniang Kabataan Chairmen within your municipality who are members of the PPSK, including those Sangguniang Kabataan Chairmen who were absent or those who were present but raised objections consistent with the rule that the PPSK acts as a collegial body and as such the decision of the majority becomes the decision of the entire organization. As to those who were not party to the PPSK Resolution No. 01, series of 2008 such as the Punong Barangays and the Sangguniang Kabataan, which is, as explained above, a separate organization from the Federation, shall not be bound thereto. Hence, the Php5,OOO.OO contribution/financial assistance which was acquiesced by the majority of the Sangguniang Kabataan Chairmen within your municipality via the passage of PPSK Resolution No. 01, series of 2008 shall only bind them and shall remain to be their personal commitments. However, there might be an instance where such personal commitment of an SK Chairman to the PPSK may also bind and become obligatory on the part of the Sangguniang Kabataan. This is when the Php5,OOO.OO contribution/financial assistance was ratified by the Sangguniang Kabataan via a resolution validly passed for such purpose and that the activity for which the allocation/disbursements will be made is in accordance with the SK approved budget. Sans ratification by the Sangguniang to be embodied in a duly approved resolution shall only render the Php5,OOO.OO contribution/financial assistance as personal commitment of the Sangguniang Kabataan Chairmen. Being their personal commitments, only the Sangguniang Kabataan Chairmen may be held personally liable thereto. Premises considered, we are of the view that Memorandum No. OM- 2008-21, dated 24 June 2008, issued by Mayor Victoria Lao Lim directing all concerned Punong Barangays and SK Chairmen, that Municipality, to remit

-5- Php5, 000.00 contribution (to be sourced out from the SK Fund) with a threat of filing appropriate administrative charges against them in case of failure to heed with such issuance, is legally infirmed for reasons aforecited. We hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, E A. PANADERO AUS Undersecreta Regional Director Rolando L. Rafael DILG Region IV-B 3rd Floor, Santos and Sons Bldg. 973 Aurora cor. Dapdap St. Quezon City Legal/17
